analysis: The code calls SSLContext.init(km, tm, null) within startTLS. The API documentation declares KeyManagementException as the only exception. The caller passes derived KeyManager and TrustManager arrays, which may be null. While null is allowed, the method can still throw KeyManagementException if the initialization fails (e.g., due to invalid key material, security provider issues). The code has no try-catch or validation to prevent this exception; it only throws Exception generically. Therefore, KeyManagementException is not avoided.
remark: The KeyManagementException can be triggered if the SSLContext initialization fails. This includes scenarios such as: invalid key manager configuration (e.g., corrupted keystore, wrong password), invalid trust manager configuration (e.g., truststore issues), or a problem with the SSL algorithm (e.g., provider is not properly initialized). Since the code does not validate the managers or catch the exception, any such failure will propagate.
